summary: A dice-and-worker-placement game where you roll dice to determine worker strength and use them to develop your province across four resource tracks, racing to make your wealth and fame markers meet on opposite tracks. It plays as a tight, puzzly engine-builder with light conflict, rewarding efficient dice allocation and route planning over direct confrontation.
praised: Clever dual-track win condition (fame and money converging)
Good variety of paths to victory
Scales well and plays relatively quickly for its depth
criticised: Some randomness from dice rolls can frustrate planning
Bit of analysis paralysis from many options
Karma/dice mitigation can feel like a workaround rather than elegant
Interaction is mostly indirect, which some find too solitaire-ish

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light race tension over shared spaces/tiles

scoring.why: The game ends when a player's fame and money markers meet, so the winner is determined by race position rather than a broad point tally.
